title: Clinical validation of the Swaasa® artificial intelligence platform using cough sounds for screening and aid in diagnosis of respiratory diseases.
summary: The cough-based AI platform screened respiratory conditions with reported clinical-validation accuracy.

evidence.tested: The prospective monocentric study compared cough-audio classifications with spirometry and physician-established diagnoses. It reported 90% accuracy for normal/abnormal classification and 79–84% accuracy for spirometric patterns, 76–84.5% for severity, and 83–93% for disease categories; recordings repeated within participants were not independent patients.
evidence.unknown: This was a monocentric exploratory diagnostic study; it does not establish improved patient outcomes or performance across other care settings.
evidence.ai_role: Processes cough recordings to classify respiratory risk, spirometric pattern and severity, and disease categories against spirometry and clinician diagnoses.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
